Q01.context: −20 °C is expected tonight. Concrete for the slab has already left the plant, but heating on the pour section is not fully installed.

options.Q01-A: I will compare the forecast, delivery time and heating readiness and decide myself whether to pour part of the section today.
options.Q01-B: I will not start pouring until the heating is ready: the winter concreting work execution plan (PPR) requires it. I will inform the plant and the site manager.
options.Q01-C: I will ask the power engineer when the heating will be ready and, based on the answer, agree with the site manager whether to pour or send the mixer back.
options.Q01-D: I will pour as is so as not to lose the concrete, and we will insulate the section with mats and film right after placement.

Q02.context: An experienced site manager proposes stripping the slab formwork two days early: «The concrete has already gained strength».

options.Q02-A: I will say directly that I disagree: the formwork stripping schedule must be followed, and I will not sign off on early removal.
options.Q02-B: I will ask for the specimen test results and decide based on the numbers, without getting into an argument in advance.
options.Q02-C: In front of the crew I will voice my doubt and propose checking the strength with a non-destructive method before deciding.
options.Q02-D: I will agree with the site manager: he has twenty years of experience and has stripped formwork from similar slabs early before.

Q03.context: A supplier offers insulation of a different brand 15% cheaper, with shipment as early as tomorrow.
Q03.text: How will you assess the offer?

options.Q03-A: I will bring the procurement specialist, the designer and the technical supervision representative together for a short call so we can decide together.
options.Q03-B: I will request the material data sheet and ask the designer to check the key parameters together with me.
options.Q03-C: I will take it: the savings are noticeable, and the thermal performance of such brands is usually the same.
options.Q03-D: I will compare the properties and certificates against the design requirements and prepare my own assessment for approval.

Q04.context: Cracks in the screed have reappeared on the same floors, even though the previous remark was closed.
Q04.text: How will you find the cause?

options.Q04-A: I will raise the issue at the briefing, state my version of the cause and propose checking it on one floor.
options.Q04-B: I will ask the contractor to trowel over the cracks and close the remark again — deadlines are more important.
options.Q04-C: I will collect data: pour dates, temperature, mix composition — and first find the common factor.
options.Q04-D: I will stop acceptance of the screed on the next floors until the contractor explains the cause.

Q05.context: The client's technical supervision has issued a remark that you consider unjustified.

options.Q05-A: Right on the spot I will defend my position: the work was done according to the design, I do not accept the remark.
options.Q05-B: I will ask to be shown the clause of the standard, present my arguments and propose inspecting the joint together.
options.Q05-C: I will redo the joint without discussion: it is better not to argue with the client, and the work will take only a couple of days.
options.Q05-D: I will take the instruction without argument, check it against the standards and the design and reply in writing with references.

Q06.context: An installer is working at the edge of a slab without fall protection. The foreman says: «He will only be five minutes».

options.Q06-A: Without getting into an argument, I will immediately inform the occupational safety engineer and record the violation.
options.Q06-B: This is another supervisor's crew: I will point it out to him at the evening briefing, in front of everyone and with an example.
options.Q06-C: I will personally stop the installer and not let him continue without fall protection; the argument with the foreman can wait.
options.Q06-D: I will demand that the foreman stop the worker and check that the harness is on.

Q07.context: At the briefing the manager asks how to speed up shift handover. You have an idea, but it still needs work.

options.Q07-A: I will briefly present the idea and ask interested colleagues to refine it with me.
options.Q07-B: First I will discuss the idea with the shift supervisors, and at the next briefing we will propose it together.
options.Q07-C: I will present the idea right away and offer to trial it on my section under my own responsibility.
options.Q07-D: I will stay silent for now: first I will quietly test the idea myself over a couple of shifts and propose it once I am sure of the result.

Q08.context: For the first time you have been appointed responsible for accepting a floor from a subcontractor.

options.Q08-A: I will ask that this time the acceptance be handed to an experienced engineer, while I walk alongside and watch how he works.
options.Q08-B: I will take it on right away: I will figure things out as I go and resolve questions on the spot.
options.Q08-C: I will accept the task, draw up my own checklist based on the regulations and agree it with the manager before acceptance.
options.Q08-D: First I will study the regulations and ask an experienced engineer to go through the first floor together with me.

Q09.context: There is a week left before handing the stage over to the client, and you see that your section is 2–3 days behind.

options.Q09-A: I will immediately report the risk, its cause and my catch-up plan with new dates to the manager.
options.Q09-B: I will warn the manager and, together with the crew, work out which tasks can be done in parallel.
options.Q09-C: I will arrange help from an adjacent crew and tell the manager once it becomes clear whether we will make it.
options.Q09-D: I will not raise an alarm: I will ask the crew to work at the weekend, and most likely we will make the deadline.

Q10.context: The work area needs to be handed over to the finishers, but some of the concealed work has not yet been checked.

options.Q10-A: I will hand everything over now and prepare the certificates later: a reliable crew did these joints, and everything is usually fine there.
options.Q10-B: I will hand over the work area now, and we will go through the unchecked items together with the finishers as work proceeds.
options.Q10-C: I will not hand over the work area until I check all items and sign the certificates, even if the finishers have to wait.
options.Q10-D: I will agree with the finishers which rooms I hand over now and which after the check, and record this.

Q11.context: Concealed work certificates and as-built documentation are two weeks behind.

options.Q11-A: I will make a list of the missing documents, check it with the technical department and spread the work over the days.
options.Q11-B: I will set aside an hour at the end of each day and complete the documents in order, starting with the oldest.
options.Q11-C: First I will find out which certificates are holding up subsequent work and acceptance, and complete them first.
options.Q11-D: The main thing now is construction: I will put all the certificates together at once before the next inspection and restore the data from photos.

Q12.context: A new worker in the crew skips the morning safety briefing, saying he already knows everything.

options.Q12-A: I will talk to him after the shift, find out the reason and ask an experienced worker to take him under his wing.
options.Q12-B: I will explain why the briefing matters, agree with him that he must attend from tomorrow, and check that he does.
options.Q12-C: I will not intervene: he is experienced, and the foreman is responsible for briefings in the crew, it is his area.
options.Q12-D: I will not allow him to work without the briefing and will note the violation in the log.

Q13.context: An adjacent electricians' crew is behind schedule, and this is delaying finishing on your floor.

options.Q13-A: This is their area of responsibility: I will move my people to another floor and wait.
options.Q13-B: I will offer my workers to help them with supporting tasks so they can finish the floor sooner.
options.Q13-C: I will figure out where the electricians' bottleneck is and prepare an option for rearranging the work for the manager.
options.Q13-D: I will meet their foreman, find the cause of the delay together and agree on what I will do to help.

Q14.context: A lot of rebar offcuts that could be put to use have accumulated in the site warehouse.

options.Q14-A: I will order the offcuts to be used for embedded parts on my section myself and then show the savings.
options.Q14-B: I will tell the procurement specialist and the foremen and propose that we calculate together how much can be used.
options.Q14-C: I will not get distracted: a dedicated person is in charge of the warehouse and material write-offs, he will decide.
options.Q14-D: I will prepare a short calculation and propose to the manager a trial in one work section with the crew's participation.

Q15.context: The contractor and your team interpret responsibility for addressing the facade remarks differently.
Q15.text: How will you organise the work?

options.Q15-A: I will pull out the contract and the design, determine the area of responsibility and send the contractor a letter.
options.Q15-B: I will forward the defect remarks to the contractor in an official letter and wait for a reply before discussing anything.
options.Q15-C: I will bring both sides together on site and we will agree who does what and by when.
options.Q15-D: I will check the contract and immediately meet the contractor to agree the division of work according to the documents.

FIELD_001.context: Before the slab pour, the rebar delivery has slipped by half a day, while the neighbouring crew is already ready for its stage.
FIELD_001.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will check the actual remaining stock, the critical path and the available time slots for adjacent trades, then propose two verified scenarios.
options.B: I will formalise the change to the shift assignment and record the agreed schedule before issuing tasks.
options.C: I will check the remaining stock and dependencies, agree the schedule adjustment and communicate it to both crews.
options.D: I will check the time buffer for the neighbouring section and establish a backup sequence for supplying the rebar.

FIELD_002.context: The crew asks me to accept the completed waterproofing before the required base inspection so they can close up the section sooner.
FIELD_002.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will state clearly that the section cannot be closed before the inspection and set a time for a joint walkthrough.
options.B: I will name the necessary checks and personally agree the further procedure with the foreman.
options.C: I will compare the available evidence of the base condition and set the acceptance conditions myself.
options.D: I will check the condition of the base and the acceptance criteria, then explain what further checks are needed.

FIELD_003.context: At the morning briefing two crews are claiming the same hoist at the same time.
FIELD_003.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will check the priority according to the schedule and, together with the foremen, confirm the sequence and a backup time slot.
options.B: I will ask both crews to estimate their losses from waiting and agree the order on that basis.
options.C: I will compare the duration of the operations and the impact of delaying each of them on the overall schedule.
options.D: I will bring the foremen and the dispatcher together to agree on time slots.

FIELD_004.context: The incoming inspection log has no signature for a batch of anchors due to be issued to the installers.
FIELD_004.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will set the deadline for checking the batch status myself and record the condition for issuing it.
options.B: I will note the missing signature in the incoming inspection log and file a request to complete the batch inspection.
options.C: I will suspend the issue and demand that the established incoming inspection procedure be completed.
options.D: I will check the documents and markings, then document the inspection before the batch is released for use.

FIELD_005.context: A new supervisor noticed that the weekly plan makes no allowance for moving the formwork.
FIELD_005.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will include the required time for the operation in my own schedule calculation and retain the basis for the adjustment.
options.B: I will discuss with the supervisor and the crew which transitions actually take time and propose an adjustment.
options.C: I will check the duration with the crew, then enter the agreed correction into the weekly plan.
options.D: I will include the supervisor's estimate in the plan and agree with the crew to verify the transition duration.

FIELD_006.context: The contractor asks to postpone the joint inspection of concealed work to the end of the day, although the crew is ready to close the section in the morning.
FIELD_006.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will contact the contractor and the adjacent trades to jointly find an earlier inspection window.
options.B: I will record the requirement to leave the section open and agree with the participants on an inspection time that allows work to continue.
options.C: I will take on the negotiations about the inspection time and suggest that the adjacent trades prepare a backup work area.
options.D: I will state right away that I do not accept closing without inspection and propose an available morning window.

FIELD_007.context: The setting-out drawing shows a different elevation than the latest issued working documentation.
FIELD_007.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will check the source data, file a request and pass only the confirmed elevation to the crew.
options.B: I will ask the surveyor to confirm the reference elevations and enter the verified version into the assignment.
options.C: I will compare the revisions and the survey control, then clarify the source of the discrepancy with the designer.
options.D: I will file a request for clarification and will not release the disputed elevation for construction.

FIELD_008.context: During a site walk an experienced foreman insists that a non-standard fastening of the temporary fencing «has always held».
FIELD_008.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will show the foreman the deviation from the approved drawing and propose my own way of checking the fastening.
options.B: I will check the joint against the work execution plan (PPR) and the actual loads before proposing a fastening option.
options.C: I will say directly that I do not accept such a joint without confirmation, and organise a check.
options.D: I will voice my objection, compare the joint with the work execution plan (PPR) and agree an acceptable solution.

FIELD_009.context: In one zone the finishers and electricians found different switch locations on their drawings.
FIELD_009.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will check the current revisions and the change history to establish the correct location.
options.B: I will gather both crews and the designer on site to agree a single layout.
options.C: I will check the documents and hold a short meeting of the parties, recording the decision.
options.D: I will compile the points marked on both drawings and find the source of the discrepancy together with the workers.

FIELD_010.context: The supplier offers a split delivery of blocks instead of the agreed batch; storage space on site is limited.
FIELD_010.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will tell the supplier directly that I do not accept a split delivery to an unprepared site, and propose a new schedule.
options.B: I will formalise the agreed delivery schedule and tell procurement which area needs to be prepared.
options.C: I will propose the sequence of split deliveries myself and record it in the agreed request.
options.D: I will register the change to the request and the storage location according to the approved procedure before the delivery is confirmed.
